note: Noroeste June 6, 2026 cumulative tally: 3,353 homicides, 3,957 kidnappings, 11,423 vehicle thefts since September 9, 2024 — all attributed to the Guzmán-Zambada criminal faction dispute. This revised figure incorporates all violence classified as conflict-related and now aligns with the Wall Street Journal's May 17, 2026 estimate of 3,000+. Official SNSP data remains lower. May 2026 was the deadliest month of 2026 (135+ deaths); early June 2026 tracking elevated: 30 killed in 72 hours (May 31–June 2), 10 in Culiacán on June 3 alone — Army airlifts 90 Murciélagos special forces, Defense Secretary emergency visit June 4. June 5: FGR contradicts Sheinbaum on Interpol Red Notice for Rocha Moya. June 6: Continued targeted killings in northern and southern Culiacán. June 7: Pursuit killing in Nueva Galicia; explosives cache secured in El Rosario. NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC: ~5,800 disappearances since Sep 2024.
Single worst 30-day death toll in Culiacán's history. Record 30 murders in single day (Sep 17, 2024). City hospitals overwhelmed.

9,000+ families (academic estimate) vs 1,763 families (state official count). At least 50 rural communities abandoned. Improvised camps near Culiacán landfill with shortages of food, water, medical care.

NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC reported nearly 5,800 disappearances in Sinaloa since September 2024 (as of May 14, 2026) — nearly triple the 2,133 previously tallied by Noroeste. Journalists describe disappearances as the 'primary form of lethal violence' in this war. Average 5+ disappeared per day; most bodies never recovered.
Mayor confirmed approximately 100 families (450 people) displaced. Municipality overall population dropped from 37,757 to 26,542 in census data (near 30% reduction including pre-war trends).
261 displaced families documented by mid-2025 — the highest single-municipality count in the conflict. Communities including El Palmito, El Espinal, and others effectively abandoned.
238 displaced families recorded by mid-2025. Multiple factions controlling territory simultaneously makes civilian life untenable in this central Sinaloa municipality.

More than 50 killed in the first seven days following La Mayiza's September 9 offensive. Bodies found with faction symbols (sombreros, pizza slices) as psychological warfare. Schools closed, Independence Day celebrations cancelled.
227% increase over same period in 2024. Tourist hub swept into conflict as factions contest Mazatlán's criminal plaza. Significant impact on hospitality sector occupancy.
Mexican Army kills 19 suspected cartel combatants in the bloodiest single military engagement with narco-traffickers in years. One local commander arrested. Occurred during peak violence period.
Eleven killed in Navy operation targeting Sinaloa Cartel leadership. Plaza boss Omar 'El Patas' Torres captured. High-powered weapons and tactical equipment seized. Torres's daughter released.

At least 3 killed when La Mayiza destroyed a Chapitos armored truck with a .50-caliber rifle in Tierra Blanca, June 15–16, 2025. Occurred just two days after Security Secretary García Harfuch arrived with 1,400 Army troops.
At least 571 civilians killed in Sinaloa in the first eight months of 2025 according to conflict tracking organizations. Includes non-combatants caught in crossfire, extortion victims, and witnesses.

Chapitos gunmen stormed a drug rehabilitation center in Culiacán on April 1, 2026, killing 8 people while searching for a La Mayiza rival believed to be receiving treatment there. Occurred despite active Semana Santa SEDENA/SEMAR security operations. Consistent with a documented pattern of both factions targeting civilian rehabilitation and healthcare facilities to pursue enemies.

A cartel hit squad ambushed municipal police on the Mazatlán–Tepic highway near Tecualilla community in Escuinapa. The operational subdirector of the Escuinapa police command, Esteban Gutiérrez Mazariegos, was among the four killed. One officer critically injured. Occurred despite the active Semana Santa security surge. Escuinapa municipality is a key southern Sinaloa gateway for factions pushing toward Nayarit.

Eight people were murdered in Culiacán on Good Friday, April 4, 2026 — Sinaloa led Mexico with 7 of 64 national intentional homicides that day despite active Semana Santa security operations. Municipal officer Jose Luis, a 4-year veteran, was shot multiple times while on his motorcycle on the Benito Juárez bypass (La Costerita, Punta Azul sector) — the 34th Culiacán officer killed since September 2024. Local journalists attributed killings to ongoing Chapitos–Mayitos faction disputes.

A fifth Escuinapa municipal police officer was intercepted and killed at his home on April 8, 2026 — nine days after the March 31 ambush killed 4. The residential killing triggered a mass resignation: 32 officers (~40% of the municipal force) submitted resignation papers. Governor Rocha Moya deployed 1,190 troops in response.

A riot erupted at ~5:00 AM on May 31, 2026 in Module 7 of Sinaloa's main state prison (CERESO No. 2 de Aguaruto, Culiacán). Authorities say inmates had consumed alcohol before the confrontation; sharp weapons used. Alert did not reach security forces until 7:30 AM — 2.5 hours later. Army, National Guard, State Police, and Municipal Preventive Police deployed. Prison visits suspended; FGR and state AG opened investigations. The riot fits a documented pattern of cartel faction violence (Chapitos vs. La Mayiza) extending into the prison system. Aguaruto has the highest rate of riots and weapons seizures of any Sinaloa facility in 2026.

Two men killed in a drive-by shooting on Boulevard Francisco I. Madero at Venustiano Carranza Avenue in central Culiacán at 5:30 PM on April 10, 2026. Victims were in a white Mazda; one identified as Christian Manuel 'N' (30, nurse). A 62-year-old woman on a public transit bus was injured by shrapnel as collateral damage.

Mexican media document at least nine named social media influencers killed in Culiacán since September 2024, several after appearing on narco-message hit lists: Jesús Miguel Vivanco García 'El Jasper' (Nov 23, 2024), Leobardo Aispuro Soto 'Gordo Peruci' (Dec 9, 2024), Agustín Paul 'El Pinky' (Jan 10, 2025), Adalberto Peña 'El Tata' (Jan 23, 2025), Víctor Manuel 'El Brasileño' (Mar 26, 2025), Gil Castro 'Gail Toys' (Mar 28, 2025), Camilo Ochoa 'El Alucín' (Aug 16, 2025), Gerardo Moya 'El Jerry' (Nov 16, 2025), and TikTok creator César Gastélum, shot dead mid-livestream outside a Culiacán KFC on Aug 4, 2026. A CNN report published Aug 8, 2026 puts the cumulative total at 'at least 12.' Analysts allege some influencers were exploited for cartel money laundering or content promotion, becoming casualties of the Chapitos–La Mayiza power struggle.

June 2026 closed with 116 intentional homicides statewide — the second most violent month of 2026 after May's 124. July 2026 recorded 138 violent deaths (average 4.5/day) per Noroeste's Ejecutómetro tally, and closed as the most violent month of 2026 for women with 12 femicide investigations (38 femicides accumulated for the year as of July 31, most in Culiacán).

category: Mazatlán — New Front in Chapitos–Mayos Port Dispute (Aug 2026)
note: Violence shifted from Culiacán (which historically concentrated ~8 of every 10 conflict deaths) toward Mazatlán in early August 2026: 32 violent incidents including 14 homicides and 8 injuries in the first week of the month, versus an average of just five homicides/month through June. Sinaloa accounted for 35% of Mexico's national intentional-homicide count on Aug 13 alone (7 of 20), with 49 murders documented statewide in the first 13 days of August. The Mazatlán Semefo (forensic service) reported being overwhelmed with unidentified remains amid budget shortfalls for genetic testing, prompting search-collective protests. Semar responded with 'Operación Sable' (launched Aug 8), surging 1,700+ naval personnel and assets into the city.
